prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural-language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), visible actions, and setting. Use specific action verbs and name any clear maneuvers; for each prominent person or object state whether they are stationary or in motion and give the direction of movement relative to the camera or scene (e.g., walking toward the camera, moving left-to-right, walking past, moving away). Describe body posture with concrete terms (standing, leaning forward/back, seated upright, reclining, crouching, perched) and report facial expressions or gaze only when visibly evident (e.g., smiling, frowning, eyes looking toward X). Give precise spatial relationships and scale (next to, behind, in front of, atop, a few feet/meters apart), note the density or flow of people (isolated, a small group, a line, a crowd), and indicate whether multiple motions are simultaneous. Describe lighting and shadows using observable cues: specify light direction (from the left/right/front/back/top), identify side/back/overhead lighting, state whether shadows are sharp or soft and the direction shadows are cast, and include visible surface textures or effects such as wet pavement, puddles, splashes, reflections, highlights, or motion blur when present. Keep the caption concrete and image-centered, avoid speculation or subjective judgments not directly supported by visible evidence.
